## Objective
- Finish the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Build request; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect the existing game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML interface and existing world/entity/block modules.

### Active
- Determine and implement the missing game runtime, then verify the game is playable.

### Blocked
- `index.html` loads `./js/main.js`, but that file does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining entity, structure, and CSS APIs to understand the intended game systems.
2. Create `js/main.js` implementing the game loop, player controls, HUD and screens, quests/combat/interactions, and persistence as appropriate.
3. Run the game and fix runtime or gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and module entry reference (`./js/main.js`).
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemies, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- No files have been changed yet.
- `index.html` imports Three.js through an import map and references absent `js/main.js`.
- The game already has title, pause, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens in its HTML.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a playable game.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect the existing game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the UI, styles, world generation, block definitions, and entity APIs.

### Active
- Implement the missing game runtime and verify that the game is playable.

### Blocked
- `index.html` references `./js/main.js`, but that file does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js` to connect world and entity systems to the game loop, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.
2. Run the game and fix runtime or gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and module entry reference (`./js/main.js`).
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemy behavior, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- HTML already contains title, pause, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens.
- Entity APIs expect a game object with handlers for dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.
- No files have been changed.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a playable game.

- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Inspect the existing game source and runtime entry points before implementation; this inspection is complete.

### Blocked
- `index.html` references `./js/main.js`, but that file does not exist.

1. Create `js/main.js` to connect world and entity systems to the game loop, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

- HTML already contains title, pause, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a playable game.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect the existing game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the UI, styles, world generation, blocks, structures, entity APIs, and runtime entry reference.
- Confirmed `index.html` imports `./js/main.js`, but that file is missing.

### Active
- Create `js/main.js` to connect gameplay systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.
- Run the game and verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world/entity APIs and HTML screens.
2. Run the game and fix runtime or gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI screens and module entry reference.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemy behavior, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Builds the camp and other world structures.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- The HTML already includes title, pause, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens.
- Entity APIs expect game handlers for dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a playable game.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect the existing game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the UI, styles, world generation, blocks, structures, entity APIs, and runtime entry reference.
- Confirmed `index.html` imports `./js/main.js`, but that file is missing.

### Active
- Create `js/main.js` to connect gameplay systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.
- Run the game and verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world/entity APIs and HTML screens.
2. Run the game and fix runtime or gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI screens and module entry reference.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemy behavior, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Builds the camp and other world structures.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- The HTML already includes title, pause, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens.
- Entity APIs expect game handlers for dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.

8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a playable game.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect the existing game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game entry point, UI, styles, world generation, blocks, structures, and entity APIs.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` to connect gameplay systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.
- Run the game and verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the missing `js/main.js`, referenced by `index.html`.
2. Run the game and fix runtime or gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI screens and module entry reference.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemy behavior, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Builds the camp and other world structures.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- `index.html` already includes title, pause, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens.
- Entity APIs expect game handlers for dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure as a playable game.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect the game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML entry point, UI and styles, world generation, block definitions, structures, and entity APIs.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` to connect gameplay systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.
- Run the game and verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js`, which is referenced by `index.html` but absent from the repository.
2. Run the game and fix runtime or gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI screens and module entry reference.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemy behavior, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Builds the camp and other world structures.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- Entity APIs expect game handlers for dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Complete the Aldermoor medieval voxel adventure by implementing the missing gameplay entry point and verifying the game.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `index.html` references the missing `js/main.js`.
- Inspected UI, world generation, blocks, structures, entities, and startup scripts.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` to connect gameplay systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js`, wiring the handlers expected by `js/entities.js`.
2. Run the game, verify core gameplay, controls, and progression, then fix any issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI screens and module entry reference.
- `js/main.js`: Missing module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity rendering, interactions, enemy behavior, and combat.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: World structure composition.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.
- `start.sh`: Runtime startup script.

## Important Context
- Entity APIs expect game handlers for dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.
- No code changes have been made.

- Complete Aldermoor by implementing the missing `js/main.js` gameplay entry point and verifying core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect game source and runtime entry points before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; inspected the UI, world generation, blocks, structures, entities, and startup scripts.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` to connect gameplay systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js`, including handlers expected by `js/entities.js`.
2. Run the game, verify core gameplay, controls, and progression, then fix issues.

- `index.html`: UI screens and module entry reference.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity behavior and expected game handlers.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, rendering, block edits, and entity metadata.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: World structure composition.
- `css/style.css`: Game presentation and UI styling.

## Important Context
- Entity handlers include dialogue, combat, shards, chests, campfires, shrines, audio, and damage flashes.
- World metadata defines NPCs, chests, shards, enemies, campfires, and shrines; interactions and combat callbacks are invoked from `EntityManager`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Implement missing `js/main.js` as Aldermoor’s gameplay entry point, connecting existing systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

## Requirements
- Proceed without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Inspect game systems and runtime entry points before implementation.

- (none)

- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, standing-stone, shard, and enemy metadata.

- World metadata includes three Crown Shards, enemies, NPCs, chests, campfires, and shrines.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` gameplay entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

## Requirements
- Proceed without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Inspect game systems and runtime dependencies before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `index.html`, game systems, structures, UI styles, and startup scripts; confirmed `index.html` imports the missing `js/main.js`.
- Confirmed no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining APIs and create `js/main.js` to connect gameplay and progression.
- Run the game and verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining APIs and startup details needed by the main entry point.
2. Implement `js/main.js` with callbacks expected by `EntityManager`.
3. Run the game, verify core gameplay, controls, and progression, then briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup and module entry point.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity behavior and required game callbacks.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, metadata, and APIs.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, chests, shrine, and campfire metadata.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, standing-stone, shard, and enemy metadata.
- `css/style.css`: Game UI and HUD styling.
- `startup.sh`: Startup script.
- `start.sh`: Launch script.

## Important Context
- `EntityManager` expects `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `flashDamage`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated` callbacks.
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; the world also provides `applyEdits()` and `updateBlockMesh()`.
- `EntityManager` provides `build()`, `update()`, `findInteraction()`, `interact()`, `attack()`, and `damageEnemy()`.
- World metadata includes three Crown Shards, enemies, NPCs, chests, campfires, and shrines.

# Integration guide for `js/main.js`

`index.html` already loads `./js/main.js` as an ES module and maps `three` to the local Three.js module. The missing file should be the application coordinator: create the Three.js scene, construct the world and entities, connect game callbacks to the UI, and manage input and the frame loop.

## 1. Initialize the application

Set up the rendering objects first:

- Create a `THREE.Scene`, camera, renderer, and clock.
- Attach the renderer’s canvas to the page and handle window resizing.
- Configure lighting and any scene background or fog needed by the game.
- Import the existing world, entity, block, texture, and structure modules as needed. Avoid duplicating functionality those modules already provide.

Then construct and build the game systems in dependency order:

1. Create a `World` and call `World.build(scene, onProgress)`.
2. After the world is built and its metadata is finalized, create `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`.
3. Place the player at a valid spawn point, using `world.groundY(...)` and the world’s exported dimensions as appropriate.
4. Initialize inventory and the selected hotbar slot from `START_INVENTORY` and `HOTBAR`.

Use the world build progress callback to update the loading screen. Only reveal the title screen or enable gameplay after the world and entities are ready.

## 2. Establish shared game state

Keep the state needed by the main loop and UI in one place. For example, track:

- Current mode: loading, title, playing, paused, dialogue, journal, dead, or victory.
- Player position, velocity, camera orientation, and movement/input state.
- Inventory and selected block.
- Settings such as sound, quality, sensitivity, invert-look, and tilt.
- Whether a pointer or touch interaction is active.

The exact player representation and movement implementation are up to `main.js`; keep it consistent with what `EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects.

## 3. Provide the game callbacks for entities

`EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects a `game` object with callbacks for interactions and events. Define these callbacks centrally and use them to update game state and the matching UI:

- `talkToElder` and `showDialogue`: display dialogue and switch to a mode that handles dialogue input.
- `openChest`: open the chest UI or award its contents.
- `collectShard`: update shard progress and its HUD/journal display.
- `restAtCampfire`: perform the rest action and refresh relevant player state.
- `touchShrine`: update shrine progress or trigger its associated UI.
- `flashDamage`: provide damage feedback, such as a HUD effect.
- `audio.play`: route sound requests through the sound/settings layer; respect the sound setting.
- `onBossDefeated` and `onEnemyDefeated`: update progression and any victory or combat UI.

Use closures or adapter functions so these callbacks can access the current UI elements and game state. Also make sure callbacks that open a screen update the game mode; otherwise the main loop may continue processing movement or combat while a modal is visible.

## 4. Implement the frame lifecycle

Use one animation loop. On each frame:

1. Compute `dt` from the clock and clamp unusually large values if needed.
2. If the game is actively playing:
   - Read and apply movement and look input.
   - Update the player and camera.
   - Call `world.update(dt)` for world-side updates such as water.
   - Call `entityManager.update(dt, player, game)`.
   - Refresh time-sensitive HUD elements.
3. Render the scene.

When paused or in a modal mode, continue rendering if the UI needs it, but skip gameplay updates as appropriate. Handle resize events by updating the camera aspect/projection and renderer size.

## 5. Wire input and world interactions

Match the controls described in `index.html`:

- **Desktop:** WASD movement, mouse look, left-click mine, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select a block, Tab open the journal.
- **Touch:** joystick movement, drag-look, and the on-screen jump, place, interact, and mine/attack controls.

For interaction and combat, use the existing `EntityManager` methods where appropriate: `findInteraction`, `interact`, `attack`, and `damageEnemy`. For block mining and placement, use the world’s block access/edit APIs (`getBlock`, `setBlock`, `applyEdits`, and `updateBlockMesh`) and the block helpers. Ensure edits update the affected meshes; changing block data alone may not update the visible world.

Prevent browser defaults that conflict with game input, particularly the right-click context menu and Tab’s normal focus behavior. Ignore gameplay input while typing or while title, pause, dialogue, journal, death, or victory UI is active.

## 6. Connect the existing UI

Use the element IDs and controls already present in `index.html` rather than creating duplicate UI. Wire the start, pause/resume, journal, dialogue, death, victory, and how-to screens to the corresponding game-mode transitions. Connect the settings controls to runtime settings and apply their effects—for example, sensitivity to look input and sound settings to audio playback.

Keep transitions centralized where possible. That makes it easier to ensure that opening a screen also updates input handling, pause behavior, and HUD visibility.

## Suggested implementation order

1. Scene, camera, renderer, resize handling.
2. World build and loading progress.
3. Entity build and player spawn.
4. Shared state and entity callbacks.
5. Animation loop and gameplay updates.
6. Desktop input and block interaction.
7. UI transitions and settings.
8. Touch controls and final polish.

The relevant integration points are `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`, `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`, `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/entities.js`, and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/blocks.js`. No files were modified.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` gameplay entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing game systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Inspect existing game systems and runtime dependencies before implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game markup, styles, block definitions, world APIs, and entity APIs.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js`, including rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world, entity, block, and UI APIs.
2. Run the game and verify core gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity behavior and required game callbacks.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, metadata, and APIs.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `css/style.css`: UI styling.

## Important Context
- `EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `flashDamage`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`; enemy damage also expects `game.audio.play`.
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; `World` provides `applyEdits()` and `updateBlockMesh()`.
- `EntityManager` provides `build()`, `update()`, `findInteraction()`, `interact()`, `attack()`, and `damageEnemy()`.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are documented in `index.html`.
- Earlier inspection found no `package.json`; the working tree was clean at that time.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` gameplay entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems, controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify core gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Inspect existing game systems and runtime dependencies before implementation; inspection is complete.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected game markup, styles, world/entity/block APIs, structures, and project files.
- Confirmed `js/main.js` does not yet exist.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` for rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world, entity, block, and UI APIs.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity behavior and required game callbacks.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, metadata, and APIs.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and quest/interactable metadata.
- `css/style.css`: UI styling.

## Important Context
- `js/main.js` is the module entry point referenced by `index.html`; it has not been implemented or verified.
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; `World` provides `applyEdits()` and `updateBlockMesh()`.
- `EntityManager` provides `build()`, `update()`, `findInteraction()`, `interact()`, `attack()`, and `damageEnemy()`.
- `EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects callbacks including `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `flashDamage`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`; enemy damage also expects `game.audio.play`.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are documented in `index.html`.
- No implementation or verification has occurred yet.

# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` as Aldermoor’s gameplay entry point, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build the entry point against the existing world, entity, block, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `js/main.js` is missing and inspected the markup, styles, and core APIs.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing APIs and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions, combat, and expected game callbacks.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, block access, and mesh updates.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, campfires, shrine, and chest metadata.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, shards, and enemies.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; `World.applyEdits()` and `World.updateBlockMesh()` support persisted terrain changes.
- `EntityManager.build()` and `update(dt, player, game)` manage entities; `update()` requires callbacks for dialogue, loot, shards, resting, shrine, damage, and enemy defeats.
- `EntityManager.findInteraction(playerPos, forward)`, `interact(target, game)`, `attack(player)`, and `damageEnemy(enemy, amount, game)` provide interaction and combat hooks.
- `index.html` documents desktop controls (WASD, mouse, click, Space, E, 1–6, Tab) and touch controls; Three.js is mapped via an import map to `./vendor/three.module.js`.

- Implement the missing `js/main.js` gameplay entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, block access, and mesh updates.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, campfires, shrine, and chest metadata.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, shards, and enemies.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; `World.applyEdits()` and `World.updateBlockMesh()` support persisted terrain changes.
- `EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects callbacks for dialogue, loot, shards, resting, shrine, damage, and enemy defeats.
- `EntityManager.findInteraction(playerPos, forward)`, `interact(target, game)`, `attack(player)`, and `damageEnemy(enemy, amount, game)` provide interaction and combat hooks.
- Desktop controls are WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, and Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` gameplay entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `js/main.js` is missing and inspected the HTML and core gameplay APIs.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using existing APIs and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions, combat, and expected game callbacks.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, block access, and mesh updates.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, campfires, shrine, and chest metadata.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, shards, and enemies.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; `World.applyEdits()` and `World.updateBlockMesh()` support persisted terrain changes.
- `EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects game callbacks for dialogue, loot, shards, resting, shrine, damage, and enemy defeats.
- `EntityManager.findInteraction(playerPos, forward)`, `interact(target, game)`, `attack(player)`, and `damageEnemy(enemy, amount, game)` provide interaction and combat hooks.
- Desktop controls are WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, and Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.
- No implementation changes have been made.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `js/main.js` is missing and inspected the HTML, styles, and core gameplay APIs.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using existing APIs and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions, combat, and expected game callbacks.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, block access, and mesh updates.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, campfires, shrine, and chest metadata.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, shards, and enemies.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- `World.build(scene, onProgress)` is async; `World.applyEdits()` and `World.updateBlockMesh()` support persisted terrain changes.
- `EntityManager.update(dt, player, game)` expects game callbacks for dialogue, loot, shards, resting, shrine, damage, and enemy defeats.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8:

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.

15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, structure, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML, core game modules, structure modules, stylesheet, and project notes.
- Confirmed `js/main.js` is missing and identified world edit/persistence APIs and entity-manager callbacks.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js` using existing systems and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.

- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions/combat and manager update callbacks.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.

- Entity interactions require callbacks for dialogue, loot, shards, resting, shrine, damage, and enemy defeats.
- No implementation or gameplay verification has been performed; no files have been changed.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e5d5058f0ffe2BFSPlmN9sLQdt" state="completed">
`index.html` references `./js/main.js`, but that file is missing. The existing modules and page structure point to this integration flow:

1. **Initialize the world:** construct `World` and await `world.build(scene, onProgress)`. Use the progress callback to update `#load-bar` and `#load-status`.
2. **Initialize entities afterward:** construct `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`. This order lets entities use the finalized `world.meta` populated during world and structure generation.
3. **Update each frame:** call `entities.update(dt, player, game)` and `world.update(dt)`.

**Module contracts**
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js` — `World` construction, build/progress flow, `finalizeMeta()`, block and terrain queries/updates, and per-frame updates.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/entities.js` — `EntityManager` construction/build, interaction and combat methods, per-frame updates, and callbacks expected on `game`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/blocks.js` — block definitions and helpers, including `B`, `BLOCKS`, `HOTBAR`, and `START_INVENTORY`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/structures.js` — `buildAllStructures` and structure metadata population.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/structures_village.js` and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/structures_castle.js` — village and castle/ruins metadata, including NPCs, chests, campfires, shrines, shards, and enemies.

**Callbacks and runtime dependencies**
`EntityManager.update` expects a player with `position`, `yaw`, and `takeDamage(dmg, position)`. It also uses `game.audio.play('hurt')` and `game.flashDamage()`. The game object should provide these callbacks: `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`.

The world exposes `getBlock`, `setBlock`, `isSolidAt`, `isWaterAt`, `heightAt`, `topSolidY`, `groundY`, `updateBlockMesh`, and `applyEdits`. Entity interaction and effects are supported by methods including `findInteraction`, `interact`, `attack`, `damageEnemy`, `collectShardVisual`, `burstBlock`, and `burstChest`.

**DOM entry points**
The page provides `#game`, loading elements `#load-bar` and `#load-status`, and UI for the title screen, HUD, settings, journal, dialogue, pause, death, victory, and help/how-to screens. These are the key targets for wiring startup, controls, status updates, and game-state transitions in `main.js`.

No files were modified.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, structure, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `index.html`, existing JavaScript modules, and `css/style.css`; confirmed `js/main.js` is missing.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js` using the existing systems and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, mesh updates, persistence APIs, and spawn metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions/combat, updates, and required game callbacks.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, chest, shrine, campfire, and quest location.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, and standing-stone progression locations.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.
- `js/main.js`: Missing entry point to create.

## Important Context
- Setup flow: construct `World`, await `world.build(scene, onProgress)`, then construct `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`.
- Per-frame updates: `entities.update(dt, player, game)` and `world.update(dt)`.
- `EntityManager.update` expects a player with `position`, `yaw`, and `takeDamage(dmg, position)`; game callbacks include `audio.play('hurt')`, `flashDamage`, `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.
- No files have been changed.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, wiring existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, structure, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `index.html` and existing JavaScript modules; confirmed `js/main.js` is missing.
- Confirmed no files have been changed.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js` using the existing systems and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, mesh updates, persistence APIs, and spawn metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions/combat, updates, and required game callbacks.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, chest, shrine, campfire, and quest location.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, and standing-stone progression locations.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- Setup flow: construct `World`, await `world.build(scene, onProgress)`, then construct `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`.
- Per-frame updates: `entities.update(dt, player, game)` and `world.update(dt)`.
- `EntityManager.update` expects a player with `position`, `yaw`, and `takeDamage(dmg, position)`; game callbacks include `audio.play('hurt')`, `flashDamage`, `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.

- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, structure, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `js/main.js` is missing and reviewed the HTML, world, entity, block, structure, and style APIs.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js` using existing systems and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, persistence APIs, and spawn metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions/combat, updates, and required game callbacks.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, chest, shrine, campfire, and quest location.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, and standing-stone progression locations.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- Setup flow: construct `World`, await `world.build(scene, onProgress)`, then construct `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`.
- Per-frame updates: `entities.update(dt, player, game)` and `world.update(dt)`.
- `EntityManager.update` expects a player with `position`, `yaw`, and `takeDamage(dmg, position)`; game callbacks include `audio.play('hurt')`, `flashDamage`, `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.

- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, chest, shrine, campfire, and quest location.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, and standing-stone progression locations.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- Setup flow: construct `World`, await `world.build(scene, onProgress)`, then construct `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`.

- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.

## Objective
- Implement the missing `js/main.js` entry point for Aldermoor, connecting existing systems and enabling core gameplay.

## Requirements
- Proceed without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

## Decisions
- Build against the existing world, entity, block, structure, and UI APIs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `js/main.js` is missing and reviewed the game markup, styles, and relevant system APIs.

### Active
- Implement rendering, player controls, UI, quests, interactions, and persistence in `js/main.js`.
- Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js` using existing systems and DOM elements.
2. Run the game and verify gameplay, controls, and progression; briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI markup, control instructions, and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: World generation, edits, persistence-related APIs, and spawn metadata.
- `js/entities.js`: Entity interactions/combat, updates, and required game callbacks.
- `js/blocks.js`: Block definitions, hotbar, and starting inventory.
- `js/structures_village.js`: Village NPCs, chest, shrine, campfire, and quest location.
- `js/structures_castle.js`: Castle, ruins, and standing-stone progression locations.
- `js/structures.js`: Camp setup and structure aggregation.
- `css/style.css`: UI element and layout styles.

## Important Context
- Setup flow: construct `World`, await `world.build(scene, onProgress)`, then construct `EntityManager(scene, world)` and call `build()`.
- Per-frame updates: `entities.update(dt, player, game)` and `world.update(dt)`.
- `EntityManager.update` expects a player with `position`, `yaw`, and `takeDamage(dmg, position)`; game callbacks include `audio.play('hurt')`, `flashDamage`, `talkToElder`, `showDialogue`, `openChest`, `collectShard`, `restAtCampfire`, `touchShrine`, `onBossDefeated`, and `onEnemyDefeated`.
- Desktop controls: WASD, mouse look, left-click mine/attack, right-click place, Space jump, E interact, 1–6 select blocks, Tab journal; touch controls are in `index.html`.
